title: Nausea-Friendly Pregnancy Meals that Still Cover Key Nutrients
excerpt: Smaller meals, gentler textures, and nutrient-dense snacks when morning sickness makes eating hard
content:
## Introduction to Morning Sickness and Prenatal Nutrition
Morning sickness is one of the most common symptoms of pregnancy, affecting around 80% of pregnant women. During this time, eating can become difficult due to nausea and vomiting. However, nutrition still plays a crucial role in the development of the fetus and the health of the mother.

## Choosing Easy-to-Digest Foods
When experiencing morning sickness, pregnant women should opt for easy-to-digest foods that are low in fat and spices. Some suggestions include:
* Plain toast or crackers
* Chicken or vegetable broth
* Easy-to-digest fruits like bananas or apples
* Plain rice or noodles

## Nutrient-Dense Snacks
Snacks are an essential part of a pregnant woman's diet, especially when experiencing morning sickness. Some suggestions for nutrient-dense snacks include:
* Yogurt or milk
* Fresh or dried fruits
* Nuts like almonds or cashews
* Whole grain crackers or toast

## Foods Rich in Essential Nutrients
Pregnant women should prioritize foods rich in essential nutrients like:
* Protein: chicken, beef, fish, eggs
* Healthy fats: olive oil, coconut oil
* Fiber: leafy greens, fruits, whole grains
* Vitamins and minerals: dairy, eggs, meat, fish

## Food Safety
When pregnant, women should be mindful of food safety to avoid foodborne illnesses and other health issues. Some food safety guidelines include:
* Washing hands before eating
* Washing fruits and vegetables before eating
* Cooking food thoroughly before eating
* Avoiding expired or spoiled food

## Conclusion
Prenatal nutrition is a critical aspect of fetal development and maternal health. When experiencing morning sickness, pregnant women should opt for easy-to-digest foods, prioritize nutrient-dense snacks, and follow food safety guidelines. To learn more about prenatal nutrition and find recipes suitable for pregnancy, women can visit our [pregnancy meal planner](/blog/dinh-duong-ba-bau) or [prenatal nutrition](/blog/topics) pages.

## Note
Pregnant women should consult their healthcare provider or a registered dietitian before making any significant changes to their diet. If experiencing any symptoms like nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain, women should contact their healthcare provider immediately.
